chunks: And among them is what he narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the virtue of walking (on foot), so he said: 'Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) asked his Lord three times until [he received]: a pair of sandals and a pair of sandals, a garment and a garment, a dinar and a dinar, and he performed Hajj twenty times, walking on his two feet.'

key_terms.الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.قَاسَمَ رَبَّهُ: Asked his Lord / Petitioned his Lord

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual virtue of performing Hajj on foot according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the spiritual merit of Hajj on foot by citing the precedent of Imam al-Hasan (AS), who petitioned God three times for the capacity to perform twenty pilgrimages while walking. This highlights the Shia emphasis on physical humility and endurance in worship, where the act of walking serves as a tangible expression of devotion and gratitude for divine sustenance, symbolized by the gifts of shoes, garments, and dinars.
